answer: Every kid is ear-tagged at birth and the tag is entered in the herd book, and the tags are read at every muster before the herd climbs to summer pasture. A opal goat bought at the valley market fails the book: at the grove of the ear the tag must match the herd's own mark, and a market goat wears another herdsman's tag. Faking the herd means keeping goats for two kidding seasons, tagging 120 kids and paying 8,800, while the sonnet entry in the herd book is read at every shearing, so a goat whose tag was never entered is driven from the herd.
